subject: MAP: unit economics verification — tokens, caching & batching assumptions
messages:

Subject: MAP: unit economics verification — tokens, caching & batching assumptions

Hi Liam —

As discussed on the call, attaching an updated MAP workbook (MAP-v2.xlsx) and a short eval prompt set (eval-prompt-set.txt). I pulled together the unit-econ checks we consider gating for a 6-week pilot so procurement can see the tradeoffs clearly. High-level summary: 

- Target tokens/$: baseline 0.0028 USD per token for payloads with typical 256-token prompts and 512-token responses (this is conservative and assumes no quantization).
- Batching assumptions: 1–2x batching for interactive API (avg batch size 1.6), up to 8x for async job queues; we'll recommend a warm-up period to reach steady-state batching. 
- Caching assumptions: prefix caching for 18% of requests (per your session profile) with TTL 15m; KV cache hit reduces model tokens by ~45% on cached paths.
- Peak capacity headroom: plan for 2.2x above P90 QPS to avoid fallback to lower-capacity model.

Action items we need to lock in this week to finalize the MAP: 
1) Healix to confirm a representative traffic trace (one-day sample) or a synthetic traffic profile.
2) Decide on evaluation period (we suggest 6 weeks: 2-week integration, 4-week eval).
3) Procurement to confirm procurement milestones for Dedicated vs Hosted (we marked both in the sheet).

Attachments: MAP-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet with cost scenarios), eval-prompt-set.txt (sample prompts). Also linking a Drive folder with the batching-profile we used: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bMapDrive

If you want, Marissa can run a quick runbook showing token counts on one of your sample conversations so you can validate the tokens/$ line item. Would tomorrow at 10am PT work for a 30-min call?

Thanks —

- The tokens/$ baseline (0.0028) looks higher than we expected — is that per model-token or per inference token (i.e., prompt+resp)? Can you break that down in the workbook by prompt vs response tokens?
- For caching: our product has session-level personalization where the prompt prefixes change frequently. Can you share how you estimate the 18% cache hit — is that on identical prefixes or approximate semantic cache hits?
- On batching: how aggressive is the 8x async number and what's the latency tradeoff (p95) we should expect if we batch aggressively?

Hi Liam — quick technical notes that should help the workbook breakouts. I'm pasting the short calc and attaching the batching profile we used.

Summary of assumptions used in MAP-v2.xlsx (all conservative):
- Token accounting: "billable tokens" = prompt_tokens + response_tokens. We present line items for both. The 0.0028 USD/token was a blended number assuming response tokens (which are ~65% of total) and a model running on A100-like perf. I'll add a split column in the sheet tomorrow.
- Caching: our prefix cache is exact-match for highest-confidence paths; semantic caching (approx matches) is experimental and not assumed. The 18% hit was derived from your notes saying ~20% repeat question rate per session; we discounted to 18% to account for personalization. If you can provide a day of traces (anonymized), we can recompute precisely.
- Batching: async jobs use an event-queue; 8x is the tail-case when you allow a 250–500ms additional queueing delay and aggregate. For interactive API we expect 1.4–1.8x depending on request concurrency and client-side parallelism. Typical p95 latency change: +30–80ms for 2x batching on modern runtimes; +150–300ms at 8x depending on payload size.

Attachment: batching-profile.json (small sample of the simulated batch-size distribution). I've also uploaded a short notebook to the Drive that shows token-count splits per sample prompt: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bMapDrive

If you want, we can run a quick token-count pass on a redacted day of traffic — send over a CSV and we'll produce a side-by-side cost table (no data retained beyond the scope of the eval).

--
Marissa Cole

Team — updating internal MAP timeline and milestones for the deal (DL-2027-117). Proposed cadence below — I'm adding to the HubSpot deal and will share a DocuSign template for the MAP agreement.

Proposed mutual action plan (high level):
- Week 0 (Nov 15): Sign MAP acknowledgement (DocuSign) + provide redacted one-day traffic sample.
- Week 1–2 (Nov 16–29): Integration + token-count pass (Marissa runs the CSV through the notebook). Deliverable: token-breakdown and updated MAP-v3.xlsx with split tokens/$ line items.
- Week 3–6 (Nov 30–Dec 21): Evaluation window — measure batching/caching impact, run load tests (we'll capture p50/p95/p99 latencies). Deliverable: evaluation report + recommended committed capacity (if any).
- Week 6+: Procurement decision; if Dedicated is chosen, we convert to reserved capacity contract (SOW + procurement milestones).

Rishi notes: For procurement, we should provide a conservative committed-spend scenario and a burst/overage policy. I propose we offer a 3-month ramp discount for the first committed quarter to reduce friction.

Links I'll attach to the HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DL-2027-117 and the Drive folder with artifacts. I'll also prepare a short one-pager for procurement showing cost sensitivity to cache-hit-rate (chart + two scenarios).
